note: T-TRV-01 (FR-TRV-02, D-86). Basic Travel Mode content: the four travel pillars (Blueprint 6.10) with hotel-room routines and jet-lag tips, and the travel microhabits that replace the plan's daily step while a trip is on (FR-TRV-01). Plain text only, no placeholders. Invitations, never orders or guilt; about an 8th-grade reading level. Movement stays beginner or moderate; items marked movement show 'Check with your clinician first' and are never the daily step for people who said an activity limits them (FR-GOL-03). Not allowed in v2: fasting, calorie targets, weight loss, medication or supplements (including sleep aids), alcohol advice. review_status: pending until the clinical team approves; prod and staging show it only when approved (dev may use pending). Listed for review in REVIEW.md.

pillars.title: Eat Well
pillars.intro: Simple ways to eat well away from your own kitchen.

items.title: Build a travel plate
items.body: At a buffet or a menu, start with vegetables or salad, add a protein you enjoy, then a small side. Enjoy every bite.

items.title: Pack two easy snacks
items.body: A piece of fruit and a small bag of nuts or roasted chickpeas keep you steady on long days and delays.

items.title: Keep a water bottle with you
items.body: Planes and hotel rooms are dry. Refill a bottle when you can and sip through the day.

pillars.title: Move Well
pillars.intro: Short routines you can do in a hotel room or an airport.

items.title: 10-minute hotel-room routine
items.body: No equipment needed. March in place for 2 minutes. Do 10 slow sit-to-stands from the bed or a chair. Do 10 wall push-ups. Finish with gentle shoulder rolls and a calf stretch. Rest whenever you need to.

items.title: Seat stretches on the go
items.body: On a plane, train or car seat: circle your ankles, lift your heels and toes, and roll your shoulders. Stand up and walk the aisle when it's safe.

items.title: Explore on foot
items.body: Walk to a nearby park, market or sight at an easy pace. It's a gentle way to see a new place and get some daylight.

pillars.title: Sleep and Recover
pillars.intro: Rest well in a new bed and help your body clock catch up.

items.title: Set up your room for sleep
items.body: Make the room dark and a little cool. Turn the clock away, put your phone across the room, and keep the same bedtime steps you use at home.

items.title: Jet lag: use daylight
items.body: Daylight is the strongest signal for your body clock. Spend some time outside in the morning light at your destination, and keep evenings dim.

items.title: Jet lag: keep naps short
items.body: If you need a nap, keep it to about 20 minutes and before mid-afternoon local time, so you can still sleep at night.

pillars.title: Breathe and Reset
pillars.intro: Calm moments for busy airports and long days.

items.title: One-minute reset at the gate
items.body: Sit back, drop your shoulders and breathe in for 4, out for 6. Repeat for a minute. If you feel dizzy or unwell, stop and breathe normally.

items.title: Arrive and settle
items.body: When you reach your room, put your bag down, sit for a moment and notice five things you can see. Then unpack one small thing that feels like home.

jet_lag.title: A small time change
jet_lag.body: Your body will catch up quickly. Keep your usual bedtime steps and get some daylight in the morning.

jet_lag.title: You're travelling ahead in time
jet_lag.body: Going east usually feels harder. Get morning daylight at your destination, keep evenings dim, and go to bed a little earlier for the first few nights.

jet_lag.title: You're travelling back in time
jet_lag.body: Going west, try to stay up until a normal local bedtime. Afternoon daylight helps you stay awake a little longer.

microhabits.title: Do the 10-minute hotel-room routine
microhabits.reason: A short routine keeps you moving when your day looks different.

microhabits.title: Refill your water bottle twice today
microhabits.reason: Travel days are dry. Water helps you feel more awake.
microhabits.smaller_title: Drink one glass of water now

microhabits.title: Spend 15 minutes in morning daylight
microhabits.reason: Daylight helps your body clock settle into the new time zone.
microhabits.smaller_title: Open the curtains and sit by the window for 5 minutes

microhabits.title: Take a one-minute breathing reset
microhabits.reason: A calm minute helps on busy travel days.

microhabits.title: Start one meal with vegetables or salad
microhabits.reason: Adding something good is easier than cutting things out.
microhabits.smaller_title: Add one piece of fruit to your day

microhabits.title: Take a 10-minute walk outside
microhabits.reason: An easy walk is a nice way to get to know a new place.

microhabits.title: Dim the lights an hour before bed
microhabits.reason: A calm, dark room helps you sleep in a new place.
